newsitem.title: USA: Conn. attorney general seeks ban on junk e-mail.
newsitem.headline: Conn. attorney general seeks ban on junk e-mail.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal proposed Friday a law to ban unsolicited electronic mail messages and protect consumers' privacy.
He said in a statement that consumers should have a right to stop stores and credit card companies from sharing their purchase records with other companies.
Blumenthal urged the state's general assembly to enact the law, which would require retailers and issuers of credit and debit cards to notify consumers if they compile and sell financial information.
The law would prohibit the selling of this information if the consumer objected.
"The simple purchase of a gallon of milk and a loaf of bread can lead to a barrage of telemarketing calls and a deluge of junk mail when this information is sold to other marketers," said Blumenthal.
"The sale of such data by retailers and credit card companies has become a big business with huge profits."
